source: Minchat Shai on Exod 11:9 (the Hilleli vs all books; the Masorah's six, signed at Miqetz; the Ramah)
claim_en: lo-yishma ALEKHEM paro ('Pharaoh will not listen TO YOU'): MS records the split — 'in the Hilleli copy: lean אלכם; the Yerushalmi: full אליכם — and in ALL the books FULL, for it is NOT counted in the Masorah with the SIX lean in the Torah, whose sign is transmitted in parashat Miqetz; and so the Ramah wrote them' — and the census verifies the printed Masorah EXACTLY (checked): lean אלכם ('to you') stands precisely SIX times in the Torah — opening at Gen 42:14 (Joseph to his brothers — IN MIQETZ, the very parasha where MS says the list is signed), then the two Vaera stations (Exod 7:4, 7:9), then Moses' three I-alone-cannot-bear stations (Deut 1:9, 1:20, 1:29) — while 11:9 here is FULL: and the corpus notes the machinery: 7:4 ve-lo yishma alekhem (LEAN) and 11:9 lo-yishma alekhem (FULL) are the SAME forecast resumed — the resumptive-repetition pair distinguished by one yod, and the Masorah's six-list is the instrument that keeps them apart: the Hilleli's divergence dual-tracked, the stream with the many.

source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Exod 11:3 (the finals)
claim_en: gam HA-ISH MOSHE ('also the man Moses was very great'): the FINAL LETTERS of gam / ha-ish / moshe — ם, ש, ה — are one three-letter anagram read both ways (checked): forward they are the letters of משה ('MOSES'), reversed they spell השם ('THE NAME'): the Kitzur — 'the finals: THE NAME; in reverse: MOSHE — a hint that his greatness was DOUBLED': the verse that announces the man's greatness in Egypt's eyes seals the man's name and the Name in one set of tails — the run's third finals-crown (exo_06's mute fathers, exo_10's blood-star, now the doubled greatness).

source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Exod 11:5 (the count)
claim_en: u-met kol BEKHOR ('and every FIRSTBORN shall die'): the bare firstborn-word stands exactly THREE times in the verse (checked: the throne's, the slave-girl's, the beast's — with mi-bekhor the prefixed fourth mention): the Kitzur — 'THREE TIMES bekhor in the verse: corresponding to the firstborn OF THE FATHER, the firstborn OF THE MOTHER, and the ELDEST OF THE HOUSE; and the firstborn of BEAST is not of that count, for it is needed for itself': the tradition reads the verse's own arithmetic as the plague's legal grid — three human classes sealed in three tokens, the beast's station left to carry its own clause: the machine files the count with 12:29-30's no-house-without-its-dead armed.

source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Exod 11:6 (the Masorah's two)
claim_en: ve-khamohu LO TOSIF ('and like it there shall not be again'): the and-like-it word וכמהו is Torah-UNIQUE at this verse (checked; the pair's second station outside the Torah): the Kitzur — 'TWO in the Masorah: and-like-it SHALL NOT BE AGAIN (here), and like-him THERE WAS NONE BEFORE — of JOSIAH (2 Kgs 23:25) — to say: also AFTER him none arose like him, as it is written here: and-like-it shall not continue': the cry of Egypt's midnight and the king who turned before the LORD with all his heart share one comparison-frame, each half completing the other's negation (none before / none after — the superlative ladder's own grammar lent across the canon); the Kings station named from the chain, the Torah side verified.

asher KAMOHU lo nihyata ve-KHAMOHU lo tosif ('such as LIKE-IT [masc.] never was, and LIKE-IT [masc.] shall not be again'): MS — 'TWO SEVIRIN kamoha [feminine] in this passage': the subject is the CRY (tzeaqa, feminine — and the verse itself conjugates her verb feminine: nihyata, checked in-verse), yet both like-it words are written MASCULINE (kamohu, checked at tokens 8 and 11) — the presumption reads kamoha, the text stands kamohu: the sevirin class (presumed-but-not-written) gains its cry-station pair — joining the presumed-she file of exo_02 (moshe/gershom): the corpus files both tokens dual-tracked, the written masculine frozen, the presumption named.

source: Minchat Shai on Exod 11:7 (Midrash Lekach Tov)
claim_en: lo yecheratz kelev LESHONO ('not a dog shall sharpen its TONGUE'): the tongue-word written LEAN (no vav) — MS quoting Lekach Tov: 'leshono is written LEAN, as if to say: it shall not harm them with its TOOTH (be-shino) and not with its TONGUE (bi-lshono)' — the lean skeleton carrying both readings at once; and MS's own apology preserved: 'even though every leshono in the Torah is likewise lean, I saw fit to write it — BECAUSE IT IS THE WORK OF HEAVEN': the census verifies the class whole (checked): lean לשנו exactly TWICE in the Torah — the dog's tongue stilled against Israel here, and the invader nation 'whose TONGUE you shall not understand' (Deut 28:49) — the full form zero: the tongue that cannot touch Israel and the tongue Israel cannot follow, one lean spelling for both borders of speech.

The chapter's letter-file: GARESH yegaresh ('driving he shall DRIVE you out') — the gimel DAGESHED (checked), 'and so gam ha-ish, and so gadol' (11:3's two gimels, asserted — three hard gimels ruled in one note against softening printers); ke-SHALLECHO ('when he sends you') — MS: 'the QADMA is on the shin' (the fore-stroke's position ruled, checked in the token) — and the send-word carries its DAGESHED LAMED (asserted: exo_06's 93-station rule holding at the release-verse itself: the intensive send — kala, COMPLETELY); me-im paro ('from with Pharaoh,' 11:8) — MS: 'the LENGTHENER (מאריך) in the mem' (checked: the meteg holding the exit-syllable open as Moses leaves in hot anger); and the Amos cross-reference on the not-again frame named-only (MS sends 11:6's tosif to his Amos 5 note).

source: Minchat Shai on Exod 11:8 (the large-letter lists)
claim_en: TZE ata ve-khol-ha-am ('GO OUT, you and all the people' — the servants' coming plea in Moses' forecast): MS — 'in ONE list of the LARGE LETTERS, the tzadi of tze is written LARGE (rabbati), and so in an old Torah-scroll tikkun — but it is NOT so in the other books; see my note on Isaiah 54': a genuine books-divided LARGE-LETTER station on the exodus-verb itself (the go-out command that 12:31's midnight surrender will speak in earnest), dual-tracked per the divergence law: the rabbati tradition named, the stream's plain tzadi standing (the token checked); the corpus notes the resonance the lists were keeping — the one word some scribes wrote large is the word the whole book has been waiting to hear.
